scraped.scraped_description: Atlas of Surveillance is a project of the Electronic Frontier Foundation

name: Atlas of Surveillance
tagline: Documenting Police Tech in Our Communities with Open Source Research
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: Reliance on Electronic Frontier Foundation for institutional support
Dependent on volunteer and student contributions for data collection
policy_outcomes: Informed local surveillance ordinances in multiple cities
Used in advocacy campaigns for police accountability
published_performance_metrics: Data completeness varies by jurisdiction (40-95% coverage)
documented_limitations: Data compiled from public and non-profit sources with varying completeness across jurisdictions
failure_modes: Incomplete data collection in rural jurisdictions
curation_criteria: Public records, FOIA requests, and non-profit research on police surveillance technology
contributor_governance: Community contributions reviewed by EFF staff; open submission process for verified data
disparity_tracking: Tracks disparities in surveillance technology deployment across jurisdictions by demographics and geography
community_ownership: Community-contributed data with EFF institutional oversight
ai_involvement: No direct AI involvement; database used to analyze AI-enabled surveillance systems
